text: The acceptable range for a target contour will be determined by local practice
Before defining an acceptable contour range, a contouring guideline or documented clinical agreement should specify what the target is intended to include.
Inner and outer contours drawn by experts on representative cases are a reasonable starting point for constructing a candidate clinically equivalent range.
The intersection and union of protocol-compliant expert target contours are sufficient to define a clinically acceptable range.
Dose-based testing is a reasonable basis for identifying candidate limits of equivalent contour variation when reliable outcome models are unavailable.
Models of disease spread and treatment outcome (such as TCP/NTCP) are a reasonable additional basis for constructing candidate ranges, provided their uncertainty is accounted for.

Before a contour range is described as clinically equivalent, its use should be supported by patient outcome data demonstrating equivalence within prespecified tolerances. (Surrogates such as expert consensus, or dose equivalence are not sufficient)
Acceptable ranges need to be developed on a patient specific basis.

Validation for use in treatment planning should include plans optimised using different contours within the candidate range, with all plans assessed against the same independently specified evaluation target.
As small individual changes may be dependent on other areas when assessing equivalence.
Equivalence bands will only be valid for an average patient or proportion of patients, it may not be applicable to the whole population.
When an automatic contour lies within a range, further editing solely to match personal preference is unnecessary.
Evaluation of a displayed acceptable range could be used to measure whether reviewers still detect clinically important contour errors vs. edits with no impact to outcome.
Equivalence-range methods require separate validation for GTVs and CTVs, including elective nodal CTVs.
The width of the equivalence band should be considered as an input for probabilistic planning.
The equivalence range could be used for educational purposes
The equivalence range could be used for the evaluation and commissioning of AI segmentation models.
